channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Metabolization of human milk oligosaccharides by Streptococcus pneumoniae
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77970-7

It is unclear whether human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) can be used as a nutrient source by Streptococcus pneumoniae. Here, Bacher et al. report that these bacteria can metabolize several HMOs, identify genes and pathways involved in the process, and show that a non-metabolizable HMO inhibits pneumococcal adherence to host cells.
item.dc:title: Metabolization of human milk oligosaccharides by Streptococcus pneumoniae

item.title: Ligand engineering enables an alkaline iron-chromium redox flow battery
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77810-8

Iron-chromium redox flow batteries are promising for long-duration energy storage but suffer from sluggish chromium(II/III) chemistry. Here, authors use a strong-field ligand to unlock a chromium(III/IV) posolyte and establish a 1.15 V alkaline iron chromium redox flow battery.
item.dc:title: Ligand engineering enables an alkaline iron-chromium redox flow battery

item.title: Reversible six-electron tellurium redox enabled by selenium-modulated hypervalent activation in aqueous sodium/zinc hybrid batteries
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78167-8

Aqueous sodium-based batteries are attractive for safe, low-cost storage but are limited by low-capacity redox electrode chemistries. Here, authors use selenium modulation to enable reversible six-electron tellurium redox, achieving high capacity and a pouch-cell demonstration.
item.dc:title: Reversible six-electron tellurium redox enabled by selenium-modulated hypervalent activation in aqueous sodium/zinc hybrid batteries

item.title: High-energy low-repetition broadband ultrafast lasers empowered by hollow-core fiber
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78141-4

This work demonstrates a hollow-core-fiber-enabled high-energy low-repetition ultrafast laser that provides broadband coherent swept sources for high-speed optical imaging, dynamic spectral characterization, and precision vibration sensing.
item.dc:title: High-energy low-repetition broadband ultrafast lasers empowered by hollow-core fiber

item.title: Generative design of high-fidelity microstructures using physics-aware machine learning
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78118-3

This study uses physics-aware AI to generate high-fidelity microstructures beyond existing data distributions, resulting in a bimodal grain structure that enables improved strength and ductility.
item.dc:title: Generative design of high-fidelity microstructures using physics-aware machine learning

item.title: Clock neurons modulate seizure timing through a diurnal switch
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77884-4

Neural mechanisms that drive diurnal oscillations in seizure susceptibility are not fully understood. Here, in this manuscript, fruit flies show the daily rhythm of seizure risks, driven by brain clock neurons and independent of sleep amount. Silencing these neurons suppressed seizures, further demonstrating the role for brain clock neurons in modulating daily seizure risk.
item.dc:title: Clock neurons modulate seizure timing through a diurnal switch

item.title: Chiral trions in enantiopure single-wall carbon nanotubes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78073-z

Here, the authors unveil the circular dichroism of trions in enantiopure single-walled carbon nanotubes, indicating chiroptical characteristics that reflect those of the parent excitons and remain robust in a Coulomb-bound three-body system.
item.dc:title: Chiral trions in enantiopure single-wall carbon nanotubes

item.title: Salt mediated actuation of membranized coacervate droplets for regulation of enzymatic reactions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78109-4

For coacervates to be closer to lifelike constructs, transport regulation is essential, but challenging to achieve. Here, the authors report the use of salt addition to chemomechanically actuate coacervate droplets and regulate transport within them to control enzymatic reactions.
item.dc:title: Salt mediated actuation of membranized coacervate droplets for regulation of enzymatic reactions
